es.summary: Conjunto de intervenciones farmacológicas y no farmacológicas para aliviar el dolor y favorecer la recuperación del paciente.
key_points: Evaluar el dolor con escala numérica 0‑10 y descripción cualitativa.
Diferenciar dolor agudo (≤3 meses) de crónico (>3 meses).
Aplicar enfoque multimodal: fármacos + técnicas no farmacológicas.
Monitorear signos vitales y efectos adversos de los analgésicos.
Documentar siempre la valoración, intervención y respuesta del paciente.
Comunicar al equipo cualquier dolor no controlado o complicación.

purpose: Facilitar la movilización y la curación.
Prevenir complicaciones relacionadas con el dolor.
Promover el confort y la calidad de vida.
procedure: Evaluar dolor usando escala numérica y describir calidad, localización y factores modificadores.
Identificar causas y factores desencadenantes (cirugía, lesión, inflamación).
Seleccionar intervenciones farmacológicas y no farmacológicas según orden médica.
Administrar analgésico y aplicar técnicas complementarias.
Reevaluar dolor 15‑30 minutos después de la intervención.
Ajustar el plan según la respuesta del paciente.
safety: Verificar alergias y contraindicaciones a los analgésicos.
Monitorear frecuencia cardíaca, presión arterial y nivel de conciencia.
Observar signos de depresión respiratoria o sedación excesiva.
Respetar dosis máxima y intervalos de administración.
Mantener calibrado y limpio el equipo de analgesia controlada por el paciente (PCA).
Educar al paciente sobre efectos secundarios y uso seguro.
nursing_care: Antes: revisar historial médico, medicación actual y alergias.
Durante: observar expresiones faciales, tensión muscular y cambios en signos vitales.
Después: registrar nivel de dolor y respuesta a la intervención.
Reportar dolor no controlado o efectos adversos al médico.
Fomentar técnicas de relajación, respiración profunda y posicionamiento adecuado.
Educar al paciente sobre autocuidado y uso de analgesia bajo demanda.
documentation: Hora y fecha de la valoración inicial del dolor.
Escala de dolor, descripción cualitativa y factores modificadores.
Intervenciones realizadas (medicamento, dosis, técnicas no farmacológicas).
Respuesta del paciente y nivel de dolor posterior.
Comunicación con el médico y ajustes al plan.
Plan de seguimiento y próximas evaluaciones.

outcomes: Control del dolor: nivel de dolor ≤3/10 en 30 minutos
Confort: paciente reporta alivio del dolor y puede movilizarse sin dificultad

interventions.action: Administrar analgésico según prescripción y registrar hora de administración
interventions.rationale: Proporciona alivio farmacológico rápido y permite control de la dosificación.

interventions.action: Aplicar técnicas de relajación como respiración profunda y música suave
interventions.rationale: Reduce la percepción del dolor mediante distracción y disminuye la respuesta al estrés.

interventions.action: Posicionar al paciente cómodamente y cambiar de posición cada 2 horas
interventions.rationale: Alivia la presión y mejora la circulación, disminuyendo la intensidad del dolor.

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de dolor cada 15 minutos y ajustar intervenciones según respuesta
interventions.rationale: Permite detectar dolor persistente y modificar el plan a tiempo.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre uso de analgesia bajo demanda y posibles efectos secundarios
interventions.rationale: Fomenta el autocontrol y la adherencia al plan de manejo del dolor.

interventions.action: Coordinar con fisioterapeuta para iniciar movilización temprana y ejercicios de rango de movimiento
interventions.rationale: Previene la cronificación del dolor y mejora la recuperación funcional.

en.summary: Set of pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic interventions to relieve pain and promote patient recovery.
key_points: Assess pain with a 0‑10 numeric scale and qualitative description.
Differentiate acute pain (≤3 months) from chronic pain (>3 months).
Apply a multimodal approach: drugs + non-pharmacologic techniques.
Monitor vital signs and adverse effects of analgesics.
Always document assessment, intervention, and patient response.
Notify the team of any uncontrolled pain or complications.

purpose: Promote comfort and quality of life.
procedure: Assess pain using a numeric scale and describe quality, location, and modifying factors.
Identify causes and triggers (surgery, injury, inflammation).
Select pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic interventions per medical order.
Administer analgesic and apply complementary techniques.
Adjust the plan based on patient response.
safety: Verify allergies and contraindications to analgesics.
Monitor heart rate, blood pressure, and level of consciousness.
Observe signs of respiratory depression or excessive sedation.
Respect maximum doses and dosing intervals.
Keep patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) equipment calibrated and clean.
Educate the patient on side effects and safe use.
nursing_care: Before: review medical history, current medications, and allergies.
During: observe facial expressions, muscle tension, and vital sign changes.
After: record pain level and response to intervention.
Report uncontrolled pain or adverse effects to the physician.
Encourage relaxation techniques, deep breathing, and proper positioning.
Educate the patient on self-care and on-demand analgesia.
documentation: Time and date of initial pain assessment.
Pain scale, qualitative description, and modifying factors.
Patient response and subsequent pain level.
Communication with the physician and plan adjustments.

outcomes: Pain control: pain level ≤3/10 within 30 minutes
Comfort: patient reports pain relief and can mobilize without difficulty

interventions.action: Administer analgesic per prescription and record time of administration
interventions.rationale: Provides rapid pharmacologic relief and allows dose control.

interventions.action: Apply relaxation techniques such as deep breathing and soft music
interventions.rationale: Reduces pain perception through distraction and lowers stress response.

interventions.action: Position patient comfortably and change position every 2 hours
interventions.rationale: Relieves pressure and improves circulation, decreasing pain intensity.

interventions.action: Assess pain level every 15 minutes and adjust interventions based on response
interventions.rationale: Detects persistent pain and modifies the plan promptly.

interventions.action: Educate patient on on-demand analgesia and possible side effects
interventions.rationale: Encourages self-control and adherence to the pain management plan.

interventions.action: Coordinate with physiotherapist to initiate early mobilization and range-of-motion exercises
interventions.rationale: Prevents pain chronification and improves functional recovery.

summary.0.quote: Postoperative pain management is an integral aspect of patient care, comprising various strategies designed to mitigate discomfort and promote recovery.

sections.purpose.0.quote: Depending on the patient’s pain, nurses can implement various therapies to alleviate discomfort and aid recovery, including administering analgesic drugs as prescribed or encouraging nonpharmacological techniques such as positioning, relaxation techniques, or distraction methods to promote patient comfort.

sections.purpose.3.quote: Pain management should include different interventions and focus on helping patients improve their quality of life (National Center for Injury Prevention and Control, 2022).

sections.procedure.0.quote: The numeric pain scale is used most often, having the patient rate their current pain on a scale of 0–10 with zero being no pain and ten being the worst pain they have ever felt.

sections.procedure.1.quote: As patients wake from anesthesia, they frequently experience various degrees of discomfort caused by surgery, necessitating an extensive and tailored postoperative pain management plan developed in collaboration with the patient’s health-care providers.

sections.procedure.3.quote: Depending on the patient’s pain, nurses can implement various therapies to alleviate discomfort and aid recovery, including administering analgesic drugs as prescribed or encouraging nonpharmacological techniques such as positioning, relaxation techniques, or distraction methods to promote patient comfort.

sections.procedure.5.quote: By using the correct type of assessment scale, and a medical interpreter to address the communication barrier, I helped to ensure that Juan’s pain was accurately evaluated and that his pain medication was adjusted accordingly.

sections.safety.0.quote: Allergies, infection, increased intracranial pressure, chronic kidney failure, and bleeding disorders are also contraindications for PCA (Pastino & Lakra, 2023).

sections.safety.2.quote: These pump settings, and the design of the system requiring the patient to be alert enough to press the button, are safety measures to prevent overmedication that can cause sedation and respiratory depression.

sections.safety.3.quote: However, the pump is programmed to only allow administration of medication every set number of minutes with a maximum dose of medication every hour.

sections.safety.5.quote: It is important for nurses to educate these patient populations about the side effects of nonopioid analgesics and the importance of limiting the amount consumed.

sections.nursing_care.4.quote: Guided imagery, deep breathing exercises, and progressive muscle relaxation Relaxation techniques are used to distract the pain sensation and redirect the pain gate signals.
